identity.title: The ALPINE-ALMA [C II] Survey: [C II] 158 μm Emission Line Luminosity Functions at z ∼ 4-6

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the [C II] 158$\mu$m line luminosity functions (LFs) at $z\sim4-6$ using the ALMA observations of 118 sources
This paper is based on data obtained with the ALMA Observatory, under Large Program 2017.1.00428.L.

targets.name: ALPINE 118 UV-selected main-sequence galaxies in COSMOS and ECDF-S

evidence.quote: These 118 galaxies are chosen to have optical spectroscopic redshifts in two intervals, $z \sim 4.40 - 4.58$ and $z \sim 5.14 - 5.85$
These 118 galaxies are chosen to have optical spectroscopic redshifts in two intervals, $z \sim 4.40 - 4.58$ and $z \sim 5.14 - 5.85$

question.value: What is the [C II] 158 micron line luminosity function at z~4-6 from the UV-selected ALPINE sample, and what does it imply for evolution since z~0, models and the molecular gas density?

evidence.quote: What is the volume density of [C II] emitters at $z \sim 4 - 6$? What is the [C II] line luminosity function (LF) at $z\sim 4 - 6$?
This paper is based on data obtained with the ALMA Observatory, under Large Program 2017.1.00428.L.
obtaining the [C II] spectral line and continuum observations with ALMA band 7 (275 - 373 GHz) for 118 main sequence galaxies
the [C II] 158$\mu$m line is considered the best probe of gas content in galaxies at redshift $>4$ when this transition moves into the ALMA band 7

analysis_steps.goal: Adopt total [C II] fluxes and luminosities

method.value: Use f_fit total fluxes from Béthermin et al. 2020 without deblending; close components (<=1'') merged

evidence.quote: For this paper, we computed the LFs using $f_{fit}$ and $f_{clipped}$.
75 [C II] emission lines with the peak flux to noise ratio $\rm SNR_{peak}\geq3.5\sigma$ and 43 non-detections ($<3.5\sigma$)

validation.value: Compared f_clipped vs f_fit LFs; differences within errors

evidence.loc: 4.1 Measurements based on the ALPINE UV sample
evidence.quote: Figure [5] compares the LFs using $f_{fit}$ (which we adopt throughout this paper) and $f_{clipped}$. Within the errors, the difference is not significant.

analysis_steps.goal: Compute [C II] LF with UV incompleteness correction

method.value: Modified 1/Vmax: phi_i = 1/Δlog L × Σ C_UV,j / V_[CII],j, with C_UV from the ratio of expected UV galaxies (UV LF) to ALPINE UV galaxies per M_UV bin (width 0.5, interpolated)

evidence.quote: The reader will note that this equation is just a modified $1/V_{max}$ method (cite: Schmidt1968). However, this is not the true $1/V_{max}$ method because the calculation is pegged directly to the published UV LF

key_parameters.value: redshift slices 4.403-4.585 and 5.135-5.85; luminosity bins 0.5 dex

evidence.quote: $z_{lower}$ and $z_{upper}$ set as $4.403 - 4.585$ and $5.135 - 5.85$ respectively for the two slices
we adopted $A=2$ sq.deg (size of the COSMOS field) but this assumption cancels out in the LF calcualtion

validation.value: Alternative method spreading UV LF number density across L_[CII] bins via the M_UV-L_[CII] distribution gave fully consistent results; different binning consistent

evidence.loc: 4.1 Measurements based on the ALPINE UV sample
evidence.quote: The results are fully consistent with our method described above.

method.value: Error propagation of Poisson errors on N (Gehrels 1986) and C_UV error from 1000 Poisson draws per UV bin

evidence.quote: the error on $C_{UV}$ is derived from the standard deviation of the expected number of galaxies per UV magnitude bin calculated from 1000 Poisson draws per bin

method.value: Assign non-detections a luminosity of 3σ using whichever of aggressive/normal/secure noise maximizes counts in each bin; gives upper limits in the two lowest bins

evidence.quote: we take the non-detections noise estimates, $\sigma$, and assign them a maximum luminosity of 3$\sigma$.

analysis_steps.goal: Convert FIR and CO LFs to [C II] LFs

method.value: L_IR/L_250um=38.5, L_IR/L_FIR=1.3, log(L_FIR/L_[CII])=2.69; CO(2-1)/CO(1-0)=1; log L'_CO/L_[CII]=0.9 from log(L_[CII]/L_CO(1-0))=3.6

evidence.quote: we have the ratio of $\rm \log_{10}[L^{\prime}_{CO(1-0)}/L_{[CII]}] = 0.9$, which is used to convert the CO(1-0) LF

findings_qualitative.value: UV-selected LFs are lower limits, consistent with z~0 LF at 10^8.25-10^9.75 Lsun; indirect estimates exceed them above 10^9 Lsun

evidence.quote: These additional LF estimates are largely above our LF at $L_{[CII]}>10^9L_{\odot}$

findings_qualitative.value: Models of Popping2016 and Lagache2018 underestimate [C II] emitter densities

evidence.quote: we find that available model predictions underestimate the number densities of [C II] emitters at $z\sim4-6$

claims.hypothesis: Does the [C II] LF at z~4-6 differ from z~0?
claims.experiment: UV-corrected 1/Vmax LF from ALPINE targets compared with Hemmati2017
claims.result: Consistent with z~0 at 10^8.25-10^9.25 Lsun; possibly higher above 10^9.5 at 1-2σ
claims.finding: LFs are lower limits at least as high as z~0

evidence.loc: 4.1 Measurements based on the ALPINE UV sample
evidence.quote: our measurement is only at $(1-2)\sigma$ significance level (68% - 95%)

claims.experiment: Compared with serendipitous, FIR and CO converted LFs
claims.result: Indirect LFs lie above the UV-selected LF at >10^9 Lsun
claims.finding: Strong evolution in luminous emitters is suggested

evidence.quote: they strengthen even further our conclusion that there has been strong evolution in the number densities of $L_{[CII]} > 10^{9}L_\odot$ sources

claims.hypothesis: Do models reproduce the [C II] LF?
claims.experiment: Overlay Popping2016 and Lagache2018 on the data
claims.result: Popping2016 ruled out; Lagache2018 fails to match luminous emitters

evidence.quote: (cite: Lagache2018) model is much improved, but still fails to match the abundant luminous [C II] emitters at $z\sim 4 - 6$.

claims.hypothesis: What is the molecular gas density at z~4-6?
claims.experiment: Integrate LF and convert with alpha_[CII]
claims.finding: Consistent with Liu2019 and, within 2σ, with CO surveys

evidence.quote: $\rho_{mol} \sim (2-7)\times10^7M_\odot$ Mpc$^{-3}$. This is broadly consistent with previous studies.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Treating deimos_cosmos_818760 C and E separately was rejected as it would boost the highest bin; merged as the conservative choice

evidence.loc: 4.1 Measurements based on the ALPINE UV sample
evidence.quote: We choose to treat them as one source as the more conservative approach.

limitations_admitted.value: UV selection misses UV-faint [C II]-bright sources, so LFs are strict lower limits; the Schechter fit has large errors

evidence.quote: Thus, the calculated LF based on the UV-selected sample sets the lower bounds to the [C II] LF.

referee_caveats_inferred: Schechter fit mixes lower limits, upper limits and indirect conversions, so its parameters are poorly defined
Conversion factors (L_[CII]/L_CO, alpha_[CII]) are assumed with large scatter
Highest bin is dominated by one UV-faint source with a large C_UV
